blocks.text: Phase 1 engaged 16 organisations, whose 223 rated insight statements span all 18 elements of the hypothesis tree and inform eight priority areas for deeper engagement.

Engagement runs in four phases: Intro & Framing from January to March 2026, sense-making and validation from April to May, strategy socialisation from June to July and strategy mobilisation from August into October (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p4, p17). The March deck closes phase 1 and marks phase 2, a validation round with a select few stakeholders, as still to commence (p4, p15). [Phase 2 to 4 records not in hand: Letsema to supply the organisations engaged, session dates and outcomes for each phase.]

The project team held structured sessions with key stakeholders, extracted insights, mapped each to the project hypothesis tree and aggregated them (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p5). Each insight is a concise statement written by the team, not a verbatim quotation (p5). Every row carries a pillar, a tree element and one impact rating of High, Medium or Low (p20 to p46). The deck does not define the ratings or record session dates, participants or roles, so this appendix attributes insights to organisations and does not quote them.

blocks.caption: Eight priority areas, each with four lines of enquiry, set the agenda for deeper engagement after phase 1.
blocks.source: Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p14. Bullets as printed with initial capitals lowered, except the second bullet of the second area, reworded for house style; the last is truncated on the slide.
rows: Province-wide access, mobility and visitor movement

Highest-friction transport bottlenecks affecting visitor movement; last-mile access gaps across priority routes and attractions; most feasible mobility interventions by corridor and destination; how to measure mobility impact on spread, stay and satisfaction
International access friction: air access, visas and onward conversion

Priority market access barriers across air, visa and onward travel; where the province is losing international access conversion; highest-impact interventions to ease international access friction; evidence required to support route and facilitation prioritisation

Safety issues most damaging to demand and destination confidence; destination infrastructure and service-readiness gaps; climate and utility risks facing priority tourism assets; peak-period visitor-management challenges and operating responses
Product diversification and geographic spread beyond the Cape Town core

Regions and products with strongest potential for incremental growth; barriers preventing secondary destinations from scaling; most credible route-development and multi-stop travel opportunities; how to balance investment between core and emerging destinations
Inclusive tourism growth and SME/community participation

Capability gaps limiting SME and community participation; why current support mechanisms are not scaling market-ready operators; partnership and mentoring models that could improve market access; how inclusion can support both equity and tourism differentiation
Market prioritisation and demand development in mature and emerging source markets

Priority source markets by scale, yield and strategic fit; market-specific barriers to stronger demand conversion; how to balance mature-market yield with growth-market expansion; which segment propositions are strongest by market
Seasonality management, events and demand spread

Where seasonality is most severe by region and segment; event opportunities with strongest off-peak and regional potential; constraints limiting event-led demand growth; how to embed seasonality and spread objectives into activation
Digital conversion, packaging and tourism intelligence

Where the Western Cape is losing travellers along the path to purchase; digital and content gaps weakening conversion; minimum tourism-data architecture needed for better decisions; realistic data-sharing partnerships across the tourism syst (truncated on the slide)
